    def compare(
    self,
    base: pl.DataFrame | pl.LazyFrame,
    *,
    keys: str | Sequence[str],
    by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    pairs: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    variables: str | Sequence[str] | None = None,
    abs_tol: float = 0.0,
    rel_tol: float = 0.0,
    ignore_trailing_whitespace: bool = False,
    blank_is_missing: bool = False,
    allow_duplicates: bool = False,
    max_print: MaxPrint = 50,
    base_name: str | None = None,
    candidate_name: str | None = None,
    on_fail: Literal["warn", "raise", "ignore"] = "warn",
) -> Self:
    """Compare the chain against a base dataset, PROC COMPARE style.

    The chain is the **candidate** and *base* is the reference it is
    measured against.  The chain is materialised, paired with the base
    on *keys* through :func:`fleet.compare`, and the report is printed
    through the ``"fleet.comparison"`` logger (stdout by default — see
    :mod:`fleet.core.log`).  Differences never stop the chain by
    default: the verb returns a namespace copy carrying the
    :class:`~fleet.comparison.ComparisonReport` as
    :attr:`last_comparison`, so the pipeline continues.

    Args:
        base: The reference dataset, as a DataFrame or LazyFrame.
        keys: Variable(s) that identify one observation on each side.
            Required; the compare refuses to run when a key is missing
            or not unique on either side.
        by: Variable(s) the report is sectioned by.  They are prepended
            to *keys* automatically, label the listing's ``group``
            column, and give the observation and values summaries a
            per-group breakdown.  A group present on one side only
            raises a flag; the verdict stays global.
        pairs: Base variable names mapped to the names the chain gives
            them, on top of the automatic name matching, so a renamed
            column is compared rather than reported missing.  The report
            names a paired variable by its **base** name.
        variables: Restrict the comparison to these variables, in
            **base** names, so a work-in-progress chain is checked on
            the columns that are finished.  What is outside the
            restriction is neither compared nor reported as missing.
        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance on the numeric variables; ``0.0``
            (the default) is exact.
        rel_tol: Relative tolerance on the numeric variables, as a
            fraction of the **base** value; ``0.0`` (the default) is
            exact.  A numeric pair differs when the absolute difference
            exceeds ``max(abs_tol, rel_tol * abs(base))``.
        ignore_trailing_whitespace: Strip trailing whitespace from both
            sides of a string before comparing, so a legacy SAS dataset's
            padded values equal the chain's stripped ones.  Leading
            whitespace still differs.
        blank_is_missing: Read an empty string as null on both sides,
            keys included, as SAS does.  Off by default.
        allow_duplicates: Pair duplicate keys by their position within
            each key group instead of refusing to run; the report then
            counts them, raises ``duplicate_keys`` and warns.
        max_print: Print limits for the text report (differences per
            variable, a ``(per_variable, total)`` pair, or ``None`` for
            everything).  The report's listing is never truncated.
        base_name: Label for the base in the report, when known.
        candidate_name: Label for the chain in the report, when known.
        on_fail: What to do when the datasets differ — ``"warn"``
            (default) emits a ``UserWarning`` and continues,
            ``"raise"`` raises
            :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.ComparisonFailed`,
            ``"ignore"`` continues silently.

    Returns:
        Self: A namespace copy carrying the report in
            ``last_comparison`` (for continued chaining).

    Raises:
        ComparisonFailed: When the datasets differ and
            ``on_fail="raise"``.  A subclass of ``ComparisonError``.
        ComparisonError: When the comparison cannot run (a key
            missing, duplicated or of an incompatible type).
        DerivationError: On an invalid *on_fail* value.

    Examples:
        Prove an independently programmed ADAE matches its base, and
        keep chaining::

            adae_qc = (
                ae_df.adam.occds
                .source("USUBJID")
                .source("AESEQ")
                .compare(adae_prod, keys=["USUBJID", "AESEQ"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Gate a CI script on the comparison outcome::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam.adsl
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", on_fail="raise")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Absorb the engine noise of a legacy SAS dataset without hiding
        a real difference::

            advs = (
                vs_df.adam
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(
                    advs_legacy,
                    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISITN"],
                    rel_tol=1e-9,
                    ignore_trailing_whitespace=True,
                )
                .to_frame()
            )

        Section the comparison by treatment arm, so a difference in one
        arm stands out::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam.adsl
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(adsl_prod, keys="USUBJID", by="TRT01P")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Check a work-in-progress chain on the variables that are
        finished, one of which the base names differently::

            advs = (
                vs_df.adam
                .source("USUBJID")
                .compare(
                    advs_prod,
                    keys=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
                    pairs={"AVAL": "RESULT"},
                    variables=["AVAL", "AVISIT"],
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.comparison import compare as compare_frames

    _check_on_fail("compare", on_fail)
    frame = self.to_frame()
    report = compare_frames(
        base,
        frame,
        keys=keys,
        by=by,
        pairs=pairs,
        variables=variables,
        abs_tol=abs_tol,
        rel_tol=rel_tol,
        ignore_trailing_whitespace=ignore_trailing_whitespace,
        blank_is_missing=blank_is_missing,
        allow_duplicates=allow_duplicates,
        max_print=max_print,
        base_name=base_name,
        candidate_name=candidate_name,
    )
    report.print_report()

    new = self._materialise_then(frame)
    new._last_comparison = report
    if not report.is_equal:
        summary = f"{report.summary}. Access details via .last_comparison."
        _settle_on_fail(on_fail, summary, ComparisonFailed)
    return new

    columns=None,
    *,

    dataset=None,
    drop_pattern="^_"
)

    Select and reorder columns (lazily — nothing is materialised).

    Resolution order:

    1. spec + dataset: derive the ordered column list from a define.yaml. Only columns present in the frame are kept.
    2. columns: explicit list to keep (in that order).
    3. Neither: keep all current columns (subject to drop_pattern).

    With a spec on an ADaM namespace, a text column the define types date becomes the date part of a complete date, and one typed datetime the date-time of a value with hours and minutes. Anything else becomes null, with one warning at collect: select never imputes. SDTM columns and every *DTC stay text, because --DTC is character (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4).

    drop_pattern (default r"^_"): regex applied before the explicit selection — columns whose names match are removed. This enforces the convention that _-prefixed columns are scratch variables. Set to None to disable (e.g. during debugging). A scratch name listed in columns is removed too, unless drop_pattern=None.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    columns str | list[str] | None

    Explicit list of columns to keep (in order). A single string is one column name.

    		 None
    spec str | Path | None

    Path to a define.yaml file.

    		 None
    dataset str | None

    Dataset name within the spec.

    		 None
    drop_pattern str | None

    Regex for columns to auto-drop.

    		 '^_'

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    Self Self

    A fresh namespace continuing from the selected plan.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    DerivationError

    When a name in columns is not in the frame (with a did-you-mean suggestion).

    Examples:

    Keep only spec columns::

    dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .select(spec="specs/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
    .to_frame()
)

    def select(
    self,
    columns: str | list[str] | None = None,
    *,
    spec: str | Path | None = None,
    dataset: str | None = None,
    drop_pattern: str | None = r"^_",
) -> Self:
    """Select and reorder columns (lazily — nothing is materialised).

    Resolution order:

    1. ``spec`` + ``dataset``: derive the ordered column list from a
       ``define.yaml``.  Only columns present in the frame are kept.
    2. ``columns``: explicit list to keep (in that order).
    3. Neither: keep all current columns (subject to ``drop_pattern``).

    With a spec on an ADaM namespace, a text column the define types
    ``date`` becomes the date part of a complete date, and one typed
    ``datetime`` the date-time of a value with hours and minutes.
    Anything else becomes null, with one warning at collect: select
    never imputes.  SDTM columns and every ``*DTC`` stay text, because
    ``--DTC`` is character (SDTMIG 3.4 section 4.4).

    ``drop_pattern`` (default ``r"^_"``): regex applied *before* the
    explicit selection — columns whose names match are removed.  This
    enforces the convention that ``_``-prefixed columns are scratch
    variables.  Set to ``None`` to disable (e.g. during debugging).
    A scratch name listed in *columns* is removed too, unless
    ``drop_pattern=None``.

    Args:
        columns: Explicit list of columns to keep (in order).  A single
            string is one column name.
        spec: Path to a ``define.yaml`` file.
        dataset: Dataset name within the spec.
        drop_pattern: Regex for columns to auto-drop.

    Returns:
        Self: A fresh namespace continuing from the selected plan.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When a name in *columns* is not in the frame
            (with a did-you-mean suggestion).

    Examples:
        Keep only spec columns::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .select(spec="specs/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()
    names = schema.names()

    if spec is None and columns is not None:
        columns = [columns] if isinstance(columns, str) else list(columns)
        require_columns("select(columns=...)", columns, names, where="the frame")

    # Step 1: drop scratch variables matching the pattern
    if drop_pattern is not None:
        pat = re.compile(drop_pattern)
        names = [c for c in names if not pat.search(c)]

    # Step 2: resolve explicit column list (spec takes priority over columns)
    col_list = columns
    type_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    if spec is not None:
        spec_path = Path(spec)
        col_list, type_map = self._spec_dataset_meta(spec_path, dataset)

    # Step 3: intersect with existing columns (preserving spec order)
    final_cols = names
    if col_list is not None:
        final_cols = [c for c in col_list if c in names]
        if spec is not None:
            missing = [c for c in col_list if c not in names]
            if missing:
                warnings.warn(
                    f"select(spec=...): {len(missing)} spec-declared column(s) "
                    f"are absent from the frame and were skipped: {missing}",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )
            computed = {node.name for node in getattr(self, "_lineage", [])}
            dropped = [c for c in names if c not in col_list and c in computed]
            if dropped:
                warnings.warn(
                    f"select(spec=...): dropping computed column(s) that are "
                    f"not declared in the spec: {dropped}",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )

    lf = self._lazy.select(final_cols)

    # Step 4: ADaM *DT and *DTM declared date/datetime are read from text.
    # SDTM and any *DTC stay text (SDTMIG 3.4 4.4); select never imputes.
    if type_map and self._VALIDATE_STANDARD == "adam":
        casts = []
        for col_name, spec_type in type_map.items():
            if col_name not in final_cols or col_name.upper().endswith("DTC"):
                continue
            dtype = schema.get(col_name)
            raw = pl.col(col_name)
            if spec_type == "date" and isinstance(dtype, pl.Datetime):
                casts.append(raw.cast(pl.Date))
                continue
            if dtype != pl.String:
                continue
            read = date_part(raw) if spec_type == "date" else datetime_part(raw)
            casts.append(
                warn_on_collect(
                    read,
                    (raw.str.strip_chars().fill_null("") != "") & read.is_null(),
                    lambda n, values, c=col_name, t=spec_type: (
                        f"select(spec=): {n} value(s) of {c} are not a complete {t} and "
                        "become null; select never imputes, so use .date(impute=) for a "
                        f"SAP rule. Values: {values}"
                    ),
                    dtype=pl.Date if spec_type == "date" else pl.Datetime("us"),
                    shown=raw,
                ).alias(col_name)
            )
        if casts:
            lf = lf.with_columns(casts)

    return self._with_lazy(lf)

    from_spec ¶

    from_spec(
    spec_path,
    *,
    dataset=None,
    only=None,
    omit=None,
    strict=True,
    overwrite=False
)

    Build a derivation pipeline from a YAML specification file.

    Reads either a define.yaml (top-level datasets list where each variable carries a derivation block) or a simplified single-dataset spec (top-level variables list). Every algorithm: is resolved through the central spec registry (:mod:fleet.core.spec_registry), validated against its strict per-algorithm model, and executed via the matching namespace verb.

    A top-level ct: block opts the spec into controlled-terminology validation::

    ct:
  validate: true
  file: ct/cdisc_ct.yaml   # optional — loaded into the CT cache

    With validate: true every assign that has a codelist (ct:, or the variable's codelist:) runs with validate_values=True: out-of-codelist values emit the standard warning naming dataset, variable, and codelist.

    A derivation block is the verb call: algorithm: is the verb name and the keys are its keyword arguments (ADR-0008). An assign without ct: on a variable with codelist: checks its values against that codelist.

    Inside a study, a ct: ID resolves to the class of that ID in the study's generated codelists.py (found from the first study_config.yaml above the spec's folder), so a spec step checks the same terms as assign(..., ct=<class>); an ID the file lacks falls back to the CT loaded in :func:fleet.get_validator. A codelists.py that disagrees with the study warns once per process (see :mod:fleet.ct.study_codelists).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    spec_path str | Path

    Path to the YAML specification file.

    		 required
    dataset str | None

    Dataset to execute from a multi-dataset define.yaml (e.g. dataset="DM"). May be omitted when the file contains a single dataset.

    		 None
    only list[str] | None

    Optional allow-list — process only these variable names.

    		 None
    omit list[str] | None

    Optional deny-list — skip these variable names; useful to override a spec variable with custom inline logic. Mutually exclusive with only.

    		 None
    strict bool

    When True (default) an unknown algorithm: raises :class:~fleet.core.exceptions.SpecError. Pass False to restore the legacy warn-and-skip behaviour.

    		 True
    overwrite bool

    When True, allow spec variables to overwrite columns that already exist in the frame. By default an overwrite raises SpecError unless the derivation is a declared carry-through (its source column is the target).

    		 False

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    Self Self

    A namespace pre-loaded with all spec-driven derivations; call .to_frame() to materialise.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    SpecError

    On unknown algorithms (strict mode), invalid or misspelled derivation fields, column overwrites, unknown fleet_spec_version, a merge block that does not give its variable, a name in only or omit that is not a spec variable, a dataset that a simplified spec does not describe, or any error raised while executing a variable or resolving its schema — always naming file, dataset, and variable. A type error that the schema does not show (text minus text, text compared with a number) appears only at to_frame(), with no spec context.
    ValueError

    When both only and omit are given, or when dataset is required/unknown.

    Examples:

    Build and materialise the DM domain from a spec::

    dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
    .to_frame()
)

    Keep an inline derivation for one variable::

    adsl = (
    dm_df.adam
    .from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL", omit=["TRTSDT"])
    .to_frame()
)

    """Build a derivation pipeline from a YAML specification file.

    Reads either a ``define.yaml`` (top-level ``datasets`` list where
    each variable carries a ``derivation`` block) or a simplified
    single-dataset spec (top-level ``variables`` list).  Every
    ``algorithm:`` is resolved through the central spec registry
    (:mod:`fleet.core.spec_registry`), validated against its strict
    per-algorithm model, and executed via the matching namespace verb.

    A top-level ``ct:`` block opts the spec into controlled-terminology
    validation::

        ct:
          validate: true
          file: ct/cdisc_ct.yaml   # optional — loaded into the CT cache

    With ``validate: true`` every ``assign`` that has a codelist
    (``ct:``, or the variable's ``codelist:``) runs with
    ``validate_values=True``: out-of-codelist values emit the
    standard warning naming dataset, variable, and codelist.

    A derivation block is the verb call: ``algorithm:`` is the verb
    name and the keys are its keyword arguments (ADR-0008).  An
    ``assign`` without ``ct:`` on a variable with ``codelist:`` checks
    its values against that codelist.

    Inside a study, a ``ct:`` ID resolves to the class of
    that ID in the study's generated ``codelists.py`` (found from the
    first ``study_config.yaml`` above the spec's folder), so a spec
    step checks the same terms as ``assign(..., ct=<class>)``; an ID
    the file lacks falls back to the CT loaded in
    :func:`fleet.get_validator`.  A ``codelists.py`` that disagrees
    with the study warns once per process (see
    :mod:`fleet.ct.study_codelists`).

    Args:
        spec_path: Path to the YAML specification file.
        dataset: Dataset to execute from a multi-dataset define.yaml
            (e.g. ``dataset="DM"``).  May be omitted when the file
            contains a single dataset.
        only: Optional allow-list — process only these variable names.
        omit: Optional deny-list — skip these variable names; useful to
            override a spec variable with custom inline logic.
            Mutually exclusive with *only*.
        strict: When ``True`` (default) an unknown ``algorithm:`` raises
            :class:`~fleet.core.exceptions.SpecError`.  Pass ``False``
            to restore the legacy warn-and-skip behaviour.
        overwrite: When ``True``, allow spec variables to overwrite
            columns that already exist in the frame.  By default an
            overwrite raises ``SpecError`` unless the derivation is a
            declared carry-through (its source column *is* the target).

    Returns:
        Self: A namespace pre-loaded with all spec-driven derivations;
            call ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        SpecError: On unknown algorithms (strict mode), invalid or
            misspelled derivation fields, column overwrites, unknown
            ``fleet_spec_version``, a ``merge`` block that does not
            give its variable, a name in *only* or *omit* that is not a
            spec variable, a *dataset* that a simplified spec does not
            describe, or any error raised while executing a variable or
            resolving its schema — always naming file, dataset, and
            variable.  A type error that the schema does not show (text
            minus text, text compared with a number) appears only at
            ``to_frame()``, with no spec context.
        ValueError: When both *only* and *omit* are given, or when
            *dataset* is required/unknown.

    Examples:
        Build and materialise the DM domain from a spec::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Keep an inline derivation for one variable::

            adsl = (
                dm_df.adam
                .from_spec("define.yaml", dataset="ADSL", omit=["TRTSDT"])
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.core import spec_registry

    if only is not None and omit is not None:
        raise DerivationError(
            "Cannot specify both only= and omit= in from_spec(). "
            "Use only= to allow-list variables, or omit= to deny-list them."
        )

    path = Path(spec_path)
    spec = load_define_spec(path)
    _check_spec_version(spec, source=str(path))
    _import_derivations_module(spec, source=str(path), path=path)

    standard = self._VALIDATE_STANDARD
    if spec.datasets is None and dataset is not None:
        named = spec.domain or spec.dataset
        if named and str(named).upper() != dataset.upper():
            raise SpecError(
                f"{path}: dataset={dataset!r} was asked, but this simplified spec "
                f"describes {named}."
            )
    ds_name, raw_vars = _extract_spec_variables(spec, dataset)
    spec_names = [name for name, _, _ in raw_vars]
    for arg, names in (("only", only), ("omit", omit)):
        unknown = [n for n in names or [] if n not in spec_names]
        if unknown:
            raise SpecError(
                f"{path} → dataset {ds_name}: {arg}= names "
                f"{name_hints(unknown, spec_names)}, which is not a spec variable."
            )

    # Start clean: the CT state of one spec never reaches the next from_spec call.
    ns = copy.copy(self)
    ns._spec_ct_validate = None
    ns._spec_codelists = None
    ns._spec_ct_validator = None
    named_spec = spec.datasets is not None or spec.domain or spec.dataset
    if named_spec and not getattr(ns, "_domain", None):
        ns._domain = ds_name

    # Spec-level CT config: `ct: {validate: true, file: <path>}`.  The file is
    # loaded into a validator of this spec only; the global one is unchanged.
    ct_file = spec.ct.file
    if ct_file:
        from fleet.ct.validator import CTValidator

        ct_path = Path(ct_file)
        if not ct_path.is_absolute():
            ct_path = path.parent / ct_path
        private = CTValidator()
        try:
            private.load_ct_file(ct_path)
        except Exception as err:
            raise SpecError(f"{path}: ct.file '{ct_file}' could not be loaded: {err}") from err
        ns._spec_ct_validator = private
    if spec.ct.enabled:
        ns._spec_ct_validate = True
    elif "enabled" in spec.ct.model_fields_set:
        # An explicit `ct: {validate: false}` switches the default CT check off.
        ns._spec_ct_validate = False

    # ct: IDs resolve to the study's codelists.py classes, as ct=<class> inline.
    if any(drv.get("ct") or codelist for _, drv, codelist in raw_vars):
        from fleet.ct.study_codelists import spec_codelists

        codelists = spec_codelists(path)
        if codelists:
            ns._spec_codelists = codelists
    # Row steps run after the variable they are anchored on (ADR-0034).
    all_names: list[str] = []
    row_steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if spec.datasets is not None:
        ds_entry = spec.select(dataset)
        all_names = [v.name for v in ds_entry.variables]
        row_steps = list(ds_entry.row_steps)
        _check_row_steps(row_steps, all_names, f"{path} → dataset {ds_name}")
    position = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(all_names)}

    def _flush(ns: Any, before: int) -> Any:
        while row_steps and position.get(row_steps[0].get("after"), -1) < before:
            ns = _run_row_step(ns, row_steps.pop(0), f"{path} → dataset {ds_name}")
        return ns

    for var_name, drv, codelist in raw_vars:
        ns = _flush(ns, position.get(var_name, len(all_names)))
        if only is not None and var_name not in only:
            continue
        if omit is not None and var_name in omit:
            continue

        context = f"{path} → dataset {ds_name} → variable {var_name}"
        alg = drv.get("algorithm")
        algo = spec_registry.get_algorithm(standard, str(alg)) if alg else None
        if algo is None:
            from fleet.tools.migrate_spec import ALGORITHM_RENAMES

            if str(alg) in ALGORITHM_RENAMES:
                suffix = (
                    f" '{alg}' is the pre-ADR-0008 spelling of '{ALGORITHM_RENAMES[str(alg)]}';"
                    " rewrite the file with `fleet migrate --spec <define.yaml> --write`."
                )
            else:
                hint = spec_registry.suggest_algorithm(standard, str(alg))
                suffix = f" Did you mean '{hint}'?" if hint else ""
                if spec_registry.is_sub_namespace_verb(standard, str(alg)):
                    suffix += (
                        " Sub-namespace verbs are inline only in this release; use "
                        "algorithm: derivation with callable:."
                    )
            if strict:
                raise SpecError(
                    f"{context}: unknown algorithm '{alg}' for the {standard} "
                    f"spec path.{suffix} Pass strict=False to warn and skip instead."
                )
            warnings.warn(
                f"from_spec: skipping variable '{var_name}' — "
                f"algorithm '{alg}' is not supported in spec-driven mode.{suffix}",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            continue

        if not algo.takes_target and algo.name != "merge":
            warnings.warn(
                f"{context}: algorithm '{algo.name}' is a record step, not a variable "
                "derivation. Use row_steps: for a record filter (ADR-0034).",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        try:
            drv = spec_registry.with_codelist(standard, drv, codelist)
            model = spec_registry.model_for(standard, algo.name)
            var = model.model_validate({**drv, "target": var_name})
        except Exception as err:
            from fleet.tools.migrate_spec import migrate_hint

            raise SpecError(f"{context}: {err}{migrate_hint(drv)}") from err

        columns = ns._lazy.collect_schema().names()

        if (
            algo.takes_target
            and algo.overwrite_guard
            and not overwrite
            and var.target in columns
            and not spec_registry.is_identity_copy(var)
        ):
            raise SpecError(
                f"{context}: would overwrite the existing column "
                f"'{var.target}'. Pass overwrite=True to allow spec "
                f"overwrites, or omit=[{var.target!r}] to keep the "
                f"inline derivation."
            )

        try:
            ns = spec_registry.execute_variable(ns, var)
            ns._lazy.collect_schema()
        except SpecError:
            raise
        except Exception as err:
            raise SpecError(f"{context}: {type(err).__name__}: {err}") from err
        if algo.name == "merge" and var_name not in ns._lazy.collect_schema().names():
            raise SpecError(
                f"{context}: the merge block does not give the column '{var_name}'. "
                f"Add it to keep:, or check that dataset '{drv.get('dataset')}' has it."
            )

    ns = _flush(ns, len(all_names) + 1)
    if spec.datasets is not None:
        ns = copy.copy(ns)
        ns._spec_source = (spec, ds_name)
    return ns

    to_spec_yaml ¶

    to_spec_yaml(*, dataset=None, path=None, predecessor=None)

    Serialise the pipeline's lineage into a define.yaml spec.

    The natural prototype-then-freeze workflow: build the dataset inline, then emit the equivalent derivation: blocks instead of retyping them. Variables are emitted in frame column order: derived variables carry their derivation: block (last derivation wins when a target was re-derived); CDISC-named carry-through columns are listed as metadata-only entries; raw columns that violate the CDISC name pattern are skipped. Verbs covered by the spec registry emit real blocks; verbs that are not spec-expressible (or whose arguments cannot be serialised, e.g. inline Polars expressions) emit an algorithm: derivation stub with a callable: placeholder and a # TODO comment carrying the verb name and sources, and a warning names them. A column that a verb added with no lineage node (merge) also gets a stub. Auto-generated by-product columns (e.g. --DTF imputation flags) are listed without a derivation.

    A verb that removes or adds rows (whereclauses, nodup with keep=, derive_param) goes to the dataset key row_steps:, in pipeline order, each step anchored after: the variable it follows (ADR-0034). A step a define.yaml cannot hold is written as algorithm: TODO and from_spec refuses it until it is edited.

    The output validates against Fleet's define-spec JSON schema; study-level fields are placeholders to review before use.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    dataset str | None

    Dataset name for the emitted spec. Defaults to the pipeline's domain context (set by assign("DOMAIN", ...)) or "DATASET".

    		 None
    path str | Path | None

    Optional file path — when given, the YAML is also written there (parent directories are created).

    		 None
    predecessor str | None

    Name of the upstream dataset this ADaM pipeline was built from (e.g. "DM"). When given, variables carried through unchanged — metadata-only entries and pure algorithm: assign copies of CDISC-named columns — are emitted with origin: Predecessor and predecessor: '<DATASET>.<SOURCE>'. The emitted YAML stays the explicit, reviewable source of truth; Fleet never infers Predecessor at Define-XML generation time. Only a column present at the start of the chain can be a Predecessor: a column a verb added with no lineage (for example merge()) gets a TODO stub and the warning. ADaM pipelines only.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    str str

    The define.yaml document.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    VerbUsageError

    When dataset is not a valid dataset name.

    Examples:

    Freeze an inline DM prototype to a spec::

    ns = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
)
yaml_text = ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="DM", path="specs/define_dm.yaml")
dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("specs/define_dm.yaml", dataset="DM").to_frame()

    def to_spec_yaml(
    self,
    *,
    dataset: str | None = None,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    predecessor: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Serialise the pipeline's lineage into a define.yaml spec.

    The natural prototype-then-freeze workflow: build the dataset
    inline, then emit the equivalent ``derivation:`` blocks instead
    of retyping them.  Variables are emitted in frame column order:
    derived variables carry their ``derivation:`` block (last
    derivation wins when a target was re-derived); CDISC-named
    carry-through columns are listed as metadata-only entries; raw
    columns that violate the CDISC name pattern are skipped.  Verbs
    covered by the spec registry emit real blocks; verbs that are
    not spec-expressible (or whose arguments cannot be serialised,
    e.g. inline Polars expressions) emit an ``algorithm: derivation``
    stub with a ``callable:`` placeholder and a ``# TODO`` comment carrying the verb name and
    sources, and a warning names them.  A column that a verb added
    with no lineage node (``merge``) also gets a stub.  Auto-generated
    by-product columns (e.g. ``--DTF`` imputation flags) are listed
    without a derivation.

    A verb that removes or adds rows (``whereclauses``, ``nodup`` with
    ``keep=``, ``derive_param``) goes to the dataset key
    ``row_steps:``, in pipeline order, each step anchored ``after:``
    the variable it follows (ADR-0034).  A step a define.yaml cannot
    hold is written as ``algorithm: TODO`` and ``from_spec`` refuses
    it until it is edited.

    The output validates against Fleet's define-spec JSON schema;
    study-level fields are placeholders to review before use.

    Args:
        dataset: Dataset name for the emitted spec.  Defaults to the
            pipeline's domain context (set by ``assign("DOMAIN",
            ...)``) or ``"DATASET"``.
        path: Optional file path — when given, the YAML is also
            written there (parent directories are created).
        predecessor: Name of the upstream dataset this ADaM pipeline
            was built from (e.g. ``"DM"``).  When given, variables
            carried through unchanged — metadata-only entries and
            pure ``algorithm: assign`` copies of CDISC-named columns
            — are emitted with ``origin: Predecessor`` and
            ``predecessor: '<DATASET>.<SOURCE>'``.  The emitted YAML
            stays the explicit, reviewable source of truth; Fleet
            never infers Predecessor at Define-XML generation time.
            Only a column present at the start of the chain can be a
            Predecessor: a column a verb added with no lineage (for
            example ``merge()``) gets a TODO stub and the warning.
            ADaM pipelines only.

    Returns:
        str: The define.yaml document.

    Raises:
        VerbUsageError: When *dataset* is not a valid dataset name.

    Examples:
        Freeze an inline DM prototype to a spec::

            ns = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="DM")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
            )
            yaml_text = ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="DM", path="specs/define_dm.yaml")
            dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("specs/define_dm.yaml", dataset="DM").to_frame()

        Freeze an ADSL prototype, labelling DM carry-throughs::

            adsl_ns.to_spec_yaml(dataset="ADSL", predecessor="DM")
    """
    from fleet.core import spec_registry
    from fleet.core.lineage import latest_lineage_of, lineage_of
    from fleet.validation.run_setup import DEFAULT_IG_VERSIONS

    standard = self._VALIDATE_STANDARD
    ds_name = (dataset or getattr(self, "_domain", None) or "DATASET").upper()
    if not re.match(r"^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,7}$", ds_name):
        raise VerbUsageError(
            f"to_spec_yaml(): dataset {dataset!r} is not a valid dataset name "
            "(expected e.g. 'AE' or 'ADSL'). Give the file path as path=."
        )

    pred_ds = predecessor.upper() if predecessor else None
    if pred_ds:
        if standard != "adam":
            raise DerivationError(
                "to_spec_yaml(predecessor=...) applies to ADaM pipelines only — "
                "SDTM variables built from raw data are Collected/Derived, not "
                "Predecessor."
            )
        if not re.match(r"^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,7}$", pred_ds):
            raise DerivationError(
                f"to_spec_yaml(): predecessor {predecessor!r} is not a valid "
                "dataset name (expected e.g. 'DM' or 'ADSL')."
            )

    try:
        schema = self._lazy.collect_schema()
    except _MISSING_COLUMN_ERRORS as err:
        raise self._enrich_collect_error(err) from err
    derived = {n.name: n for n in latest_lineage_of(self)}
    hazards = _spec_order_hazards(lineage_of(self))
    name_pattern = re.compile(r"^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,7}$")
    # The columns at the start of the chain: only they can be a carry-through
    # or a Predecessor; a column a verb added with no lineage node is a stub.
    root_lazy = getattr(self, "_root_lazy", None)
    root_cols = set(root_lazy.collect_schema().names()) if root_lazy is not None else None

    entries: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], str | None]] = []
    frozen_codelists: dict[str, dict | None] = getattr(self, "_frozen_codelists", {})
    codelists: dict[str, dict] = {}
    ct_todos: list[str] = []
    for col in schema.names():
        node = derived.get(col)
        if node is None and not name_pattern.match(col):
            continue  # raw scratch column — not part of the dataset spec
        entry: dict[str, Any] = {
            "name": col,
            "label": col,
            "type": _dtype_to_spec_type(schema.get(col)),
        }
        comment: str | None = None
        if node is None and root_cols is not None and col not in root_cols:
            comment = (
                f"TODO: column {col} was added by a verb that records no lineage "
                "(for example merge) — replace this stub with a registered "
                "derivation (algorithm: derivation, callable: <name>)."
            )
            entry["derivation"] = {"algorithm": "derivation", "callable": f"TODO_{col}"}
        elif node is not None and col in hazards:
            comment = (
                f"TODO: {hazards[col]}, so a block run in order gives another value "
                "than the inline chain — write the derivation of the value the "
                "dataset holds (algorithm: derivation, callable: <name>)."
            )
            entry["derivation"] = {"algorithm": "derivation", "callable": f"TODO_{col}"}
        elif node is not None:
            status, block, meta = spec_registry.derivation_from_lineage(standard, node)
            if meta.get("label"):
                entry["label"] = str(meta["label"])[:40]
            if meta.get("origin"):
                entry["origin"] = meta["origin"]
            if meta.get("evaluator"):
                entry["evaluator"] = meta["evaluator"]
            if status == "ok":
                # A pure copy of a CDISC-named upstream column is a
                # Predecessor in Define-XML terms; an explicit origin
                # captured from the verb call wins.
                source = str(block.get("source") or col) if block else col
                if (
                    pred_ds
                    and "origin" not in entry
                    and block
                    and block.get("algorithm") == "assign"
                    and block.get("value") is None
                    and not block.get("ct")
                    and name_pattern.match(source)
                    and (root_cols is None or source in root_cols)
                ):
                    entry["origin"] = "Predecessor"
                    entry["predecessor"] = f"{pred_ds}.{source}"
                ct_ref = block.get("ct") if block else None
                if ct_ref in frozen_codelists:
                    if frozen_codelists[ct_ref] is None:
                        ct_todos.append(f"{col} ({ct_ref})")
                    else:
                        entry["codelist"] = ct_ref
                        codelists[ct_ref] = frozen_codelists[ct_ref]
                entry["derivation"] = block
            elif status == "stub":
                srcs = ", ".join(node.sources) if node.sources else "none"
                comment = (
                    f"TODO: verb '{node.verb}' (sources: {srcs}) is not spec-expressible "
                    f"— replace this stub with a registered derivation "
                    f"(algorithm: derivation, callable: <name>)."
                )
                entry["derivation"] = {
                    "algorithm": "derivation",
                    "callable": f"TODO_{col}",
                }
            # status == "byproduct": metadata-only (auto-generated column).
        elif pred_ds:
            # Metadata-only carry-through — flowed in untouched.
            entry["origin"] = "Predecessor"
            entry["predecessor"] = f"{pred_ds}.{col}"
        entries.append((entry, comment))

    if not entries:
        raise DerivationError(
            "to_spec_yaml(): nothing to serialise — the frame has no derived "
            "variables and no CDISC-named columns."
        )

    if hazards:
        warnings.warn(
            "to_spec_yaml: the spec cannot give the inline values of "
            + "; ".join(f"{name} ({why})" for name, why in hazards.items())
            + ". Their blocks are TODO stubs.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    # from_spec runs the blocks in frame order: a block that reads a variable a
    # later block creates reads it before that block runs.
    position = {entry["name"]: i for i, (entry, _) in enumerate(entries)}
    late = [
        f"{name} reads {src}"
        for name, node in derived.items()
        if name in position
        for src in node.sources
        if src != name and src in derived and position.get(src, -1) > position[name]
    ]
    if late:
        warnings.warn(
            f"to_spec_yaml: {'; '.join(late)}, which a later block of the spec "
            "creates. from_spec runs the blocks in this order, so check the values.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    stubs = [entry["name"] for entry, comment in entries if comment]
    if stubs:
        warnings.warn(
            f"to_spec_yaml: {len(stubs)} variable(s) are TODO stubs "
            f"({', '.join(stubs)}): from_spec fails on them until you replace each "
            "callable: TODO_<name> with a registered @derivation, and Define-XML has "
            "no method text for them.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    var_names = [e["name"] for e, _ in entries]
    keys = [k for k in ("STUDYID", "USUBJID") if k in var_names] or var_names[:1]
    row_steps = _freeze_row_steps(self, var_names)
    todo_steps = [st["verb"] for st in row_steps if st["algorithm"] == "TODO"]
    if todo_steps:
        warnings.warn(
            f"to_spec_yaml: {len(todo_steps)} row step(s) cannot be written "
            f"({', '.join(todo_steps)}): from_spec fails on algorithm: TODO in "
            "row_steps until you replace each one (ADR-0034).",
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    study = {
        "id": "STUDY",
        "name": "STUDY",
        "description": (
            "Generated by Fleet to_spec_yaml() — replace with the study description."
        ),
        "protocol_name": "STUDY",
        "originator": "Fleet",
        "standard": "SDTMIG" if standard == "sdtm" else "ADAMIG",
        "standard_version": DEFAULT_IG_VERSIONS[standard],
    }
    head = {"fleet_spec_version": SUPPORTED_SPEC_VERSION, "study": study}
    if codelists:
        head["codelists"] = list(codelists.values())
    ds_head: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": ds_name,
        "label": ds_name,
        "structure": "One record per observation (review)",
        "keys": keys,
    }
    if row_steps:
        ds_head["row_steps"] = row_steps

    lines: list[str] = [
        "# Generated by Fleet to_spec_yaml() — review study fields, labels, keys,",
        "# and TODO stubs before use.",
    ]
    if todo_steps:
        lines.append(
            "# TODO: row_steps holds algorithm: TODO for "
            f"{', '.join(todo_steps)} — write each step before from_spec runs."
        )
    if ct_todos:
        lines.append(
            f"# TODO: no codelist terms were known for {', '.join(ct_todos)}; add a "
            "codelists: entry and a codelist: key, or Define-XML has no CodeListRef."
        )
    lines += [
        yaml.safe_dump(head, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True).rstrip(),
        "datasets:",
        _indent_yaml(yaml.safe_dump([ds_head], sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True), 2),
        "    variables:",
    ]
    for entry, comment in entries:
        block_text = _indent_yaml(
            yaml.safe_dump([entry], sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True), 6
        )
        if comment:
            block_lines: list[str] = []
            for ln in block_text.splitlines():
                if ln.strip().startswith("derivation:"):
                    pad = ln[: len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())]
                    block_lines.append(f"{pad}# {comment}")
                block_lines.append(ln)
            block_text = "\n".join(block_lines)
        lines.append(block_text)

    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    if path is not None:
        dest = Path(path)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return text

    nodup ¶

    nodup(
    *, subset, order_by=None, keep=None, descending=False
)

    Detect duplicate rows and optionally deduplicate after sorting.

    Materialises the pipeline, logs duplicate diagnostics through the "fleet" logger (stdout by default — see :mod:fleet.core.log), and optionally removes duplicates. When keep is None (default) the verb operates in report-only mode — duplicates are reported but the frame is returned unchanged, making it safe to insert anywhere in a pipeline for auditing purposes. The duplicate rows are also attached to the returned namespace and retrievable via :attr:last_nodup_report.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    subset str | list[str]

    Column(s) that define the uniqueness key.

    		 required
    order_by str | list[str] | None

    Column(s) to sort by before deduplication. Required when keep is not None.

    		 None
    keep Literal['first', 'last'] | None

    Which duplicate to retain after sorting: "first", "last", or None (report only, no removal).

    		 None
    descending bool | list[bool]

    Sort direction(s) for order_by. A single bool applies to all columns; a list must match order_by length. A missing value is the lowest value, as SAS: it sorts first when ascending and last when descending. Records that tie on order_by keep their input order, as PROC SORT EQUALS, so keep="last" takes the last input record of a tie.

    		 False

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    Self Self

    A fresh namespace wrapping the (optionally deduplicated) frame, carrying the duplicates in last_nodup_report; call .to_frame() to materialise. With keep, the rows are always sorted by subset, then order_by, as PROC SORT NODUPKEY, also when no duplicate exists.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    DerivationError

    If keep is set but order_by is not provided, keep is not one of the accepted values, or a column of subset or order_by is not in the frame.
    References

    SAS PROC SORT with EQUALS and NODUPKEY; ADR-0023 for the place of a missing value.

    Examples:

    Report-only mode (audit duplicates without removing)::

    ae = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .nodup(subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESTDTC"])
    .to_frame()
)

    Sort and deduplicate (keep latest record)::

    adae = (
    ae_df.adam.occds
    .nodup(
        subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD"],
        order_by=["ASTDT", "ASEQ"],
        keep="first",
        descending=True,
    )
    .to_frame()
)

    def nodup(
    self,
    *,
    subset: str | list[str],
    order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
    keep: Literal["first", "last"] | None = None,
    descending: bool | list[bool] = False,
) -> Self:
    """Detect duplicate rows and optionally deduplicate after sorting.

    Materialises the pipeline, logs duplicate diagnostics through the
    ``"fleet"`` logger (stdout by default — see :mod:`fleet.core.log`),
    and optionally removes duplicates.  When ``keep`` is ``None``
    (default) the verb operates in report-only mode — duplicates are
    reported but the frame is returned unchanged, making it safe to
    insert anywhere in a pipeline for auditing purposes.  The
    duplicate rows are also attached to the returned namespace and
    retrievable via :attr:`last_nodup_report`.

    Args:
        subset: Column(s) that define the uniqueness key.
        order_by: Column(s) to sort by before deduplication.  Required
            when ``keep`` is not ``None``.
        keep: Which duplicate to retain after sorting:
            ``"first"``, ``"last"``, or ``None`` (report only, no removal).
        descending: Sort direction(s) for *order_by*.  A single ``bool``
            applies to all columns; a list must match *order_by* length.
            A missing value is the lowest value, as SAS: it sorts
            first when ascending and last when descending.  Records
            that tie on *order_by* keep their input order, as PROC SORT
            EQUALS, so ``keep="last"`` takes the last input record of a
            tie.

    Returns:
        Self: A fresh namespace wrapping the (optionally deduplicated)
            frame, carrying the duplicates in ``last_nodup_report``;
            call ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.  With *keep*, the rows
            are always sorted by *subset*, then *order_by*, as PROC SORT
            NODUPKEY, also when no duplicate exists.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: If ``keep`` is set but ``order_by`` is not
            provided, ``keep`` is not one of the accepted values, or a
            column of *subset* or *order_by* is not in the frame.

    References:
        SAS PROC SORT with EQUALS and NODUPKEY; ADR-0023 for the place
        of a missing value.

    Examples:
        Report-only mode (audit duplicates without removing)::

            ae = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .assign("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
                .nodup(subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD", "AESTDTC"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Sort and deduplicate (keep latest record)::

            adae = (
                ae_df.adam.occds
                .nodup(
                    subset=["USUBJID", "AEDECOD"],
                    order_by=["ASTDT", "ASEQ"],
                    keep="first",
                    descending=True,
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if keep is not None and order_by is None:
        raise DerivationError("order_by is required when keep is set.")
    if keep is not None and keep not in ("first", "last"):
        raise DerivationError(f"keep must be 'first', 'last', or None — got {keep!r}.")
    subset = [subset] if isinstance(subset, str) else list(subset)
    if isinstance(order_by, str):
        order_by = [order_by]
    self._require_columns("nodup(subset=...)", subset)
    if order_by:
        self._require_columns("nodup(order_by=...)", order_by)

    fleet_log.ensure_default_handler()
    df = self._collect_checked()
    if keep is not None:
        # As PROC SORT NODUPKEY: always sort by the key, then order_by, so the
        # row order does not depend on whether a duplicate exists.  A missing
        # value is lowest, as SAS (ADR-0023); ties keep input order.
        flags = (
            list(descending) if isinstance(descending, list) else [descending] * len(order_by)
        )
        all_flags = [False] * len(subset) + flags
        df = df.sort(
            [*subset, *order_by],
            descending=all_flags,
            nulls_last=all_flags,
            maintain_order=True,
        )

    # Detect duplicates
    dup_mask = df.select(pl.struct(subset).is_duplicated()).to_series()
    n_dup = dup_mask.sum()
    dup_rows = df.filter(dup_mask)

    if n_dup == 0:
        logger.info("[NODUP] No duplicates found (subset: %s)", ", ".join(subset))
        new = self._materialise_then(df)
        new._nodup_report = dup_rows
        return self._record_nodup(new, subset, order_by, keep, descending)

    # Summarise duplicate groups
    dup_groups = (
        dup_rows.group_by(subset)
        .agg(pl.len().alias("__count"))
        .sort("__count", descending=True)
    )
    n_groups = len(dup_groups)

    logger.info(
        "[NODUP] %d duplicate rows across %d key group(s) (subset: %s)",
        n_dup,
        n_groups,
        ", ".join(subset),
    )
    # Show top offending groups (up to 5)
    top = dup_groups.head(5)
    logger.info("[NODUP] Top offenders:")
    for row in top.iter_rows(named=True):
        count = row.pop("__count")
        key_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in row.items())
        logger.info("  %s  (%d rows)", key_str, count)

    # Report-only mode
    if keep is None:
        logger.info("[NODUP] Action: report only (keep=None)")
        new = self._materialise_then(df)
        new._nodup_report = dup_rows
        return new

    # Deduplicate the sorted frame.
    df = df.unique(subset=subset, keep=keep, maintain_order=True)

    logger.info(
        "[NODUP] Action: keeping '%s' after sorting by %s (descending=%s)",
        keep,
        order_by,
        descending,
    )
    logger.info("[NODUP] Result: %d rows (removed %d)", len(df), n_dup - n_groups)
    new = self._materialise_then(df)
    new._nodup_report = dup_rows
    return self._record_nodup(new, subset, order_by, keep, descending)

    class PinMixin:
    """Mixin that lets any namespace attach reference-domain DataFrames.

    Instance attributes set by this mixin (all survive ``copy.copy``):

    * ``_pinned`` — ``dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]]``
      keyed by upper-cased domain name → ``(dataframe, join_key)``.
    * ``_pin_lineage`` — ``list[PinDependency]`` accumulated cross-domain
      access records.
    * ``_fk_severity`` — default FK-check severity (``"warn"`` | ``"error"``
      | ``"off"``).
    """

    # Namespace subclasses override with domain-specific rules. Rule keys: pin, ref_col,
    # allow (space-separated legal values), max_severity ("warn"), note (added to the message).
    _FK_RULES: ClassVar[dict[str, dict[str, str]]] = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Public verbs                                                         #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    @overload
    def pin(
        self,
        domain: str,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        /,
        *,
        join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
        **frames: pl.DataFrame,
    ) -> Self: ...

    @overload
    def pin(
        self,
        /,
        *,
        join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
        **frames: pl.DataFrame,
    ) -> Self: ...

    def pin(
        self,
        domain: str | None = None,
        df: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        /,
        *,
        join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
        **frames: pl.DataFrame,
    ) -> Self:
        """Attach one or more reference domains to this pipeline.

        Two equivalent forms, usable together — the keyword form declares
        every upstream dataset in one call (kwarg name = dataset name),
        mirroring the define.yaml ``inputs:`` block:

        * ``pin("DM", dm_df)`` — one pin, positional.
        * ``pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df)`` — several pins, one call.

        The name/frame pair is positional-only, so *every* keyword except
        ``join_on`` is a dataset pin — no dataset name is reserved.

        Args:
            domain: Logical name (e.g. ``"DM"``, ``"ADSL"``, ``"TV"``).
            df: The reference DataFrame for *domain*.  A LazyFrame is
                collected once, at pin time.
            join_on: Column(s) used to join these references into the
                pipeline.  Applies to every pin in this call; pin
                separately for per-domain join keys.
            **frames: ``NAME=frame`` pins (names are upper-cased).

        Returns:
            Self: A shallow copy with the pin(s) attached; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When called with no pins, a name without its
                frame (or vice versa), or a pinned value that is not a
                DataFrame/LazyFrame.

        Examples:
            Pin DM to an AE pipeline for study-day derivation::

                ae = (
                    ae_raw.sdtm
                    .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
                    .pin("DM", dm_df)
                    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Declare every upstream dataset of an ADaM pipeline at once::

                adae = (
                    ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
                    .pin(ADSL=adsl_df, EX=ex_df)
                    .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "SAFFL")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        pins: dict[str, pl.DataFrame] = {}
        if domain is not None or df is not None:
            if domain is None or df is None:
                raise DerivationError(
                    "pin() requires both a domain name and a DataFrame — "
                    'pin("DM", dm_df) — or keyword pins: pin(DM=dm_df).'
                )
            pins[domain] = df
        pins.update(frames)
        if not pins:
            raise DerivationError(
                'pin() requires at least one pin: pin("DM", dm_df) or pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df).'
            )

        new = copy.copy(self)
        pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = dict(getattr(self, "_pinned", {}))
        for name, frame in pins.items():
            frame = _pin_frame(name, frame)
            key = name.upper()
            if key in pinned:
                warnings.warn(
                    f"Pin '{key}' replaced. Use .repin() to suppress this warning.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )
            pinned[key] = (frame, _normalize_key(join_on))
        new._pinned = pinned
        return new

    def repin(
        self,
        domain: str,
        df: pl.DataFrame,
        *,
        join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
    ) -> Self:
        """Replace an existing pin explicitly (no warning).

        Args:
            domain: Logical name to replace.
            df: The new reference DataFrame.  A LazyFrame is collected
                once, at pin time.
            join_on: Column(s) for the join key.

        Returns:
            Self: A shallow copy with the pin replaced.

        Raises:
            DerivationError: When *df* is not a DataFrame or LazyFrame.

        Examples:
            Replace a previously pinned DM with a filtered version::

                ae = (
                    ae_raw.sdtm
                    .pin("DM", dm_full)
                    .repin("DM", dm_filtered)
                    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        new = copy.copy(self)
        pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = dict(getattr(self, "_pinned", {}))
        pinned[domain.upper()] = (_pin_frame(domain, df), _normalize_key(join_on))
        new._pinned = pinned
        return new

    def pins(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Inspect currently pinned domains.

        Returns:
            dict: ``{domain: {"df": DataFrame, "join_on": [cols]}}``.

        Examples:
            Check what's pinned before study_day::

                ns = ae_raw.sdtm.pin("DM", dm_df).pin("TV", tv_df, join_on="VISITNUM")
                print(ns.pins())
                # {'DM': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['USUBJID']},
                #  'TV': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['VISITNUM']}}
        """
        pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = getattr(self, "_pinned", {})
        return {domain: {"df": df, "join_on": list(key)} for domain, (df, key) in pinned.items()}

    def fk_policy(self, severity: str) -> Self:
        """Set the FK-check severity for this pipeline.

        The check runs once, at the public ``to_frame()`` (and the
        terminal verbs that call it), on the final frame, with the
        severity in force at that point.  The order of ``pin``,
        ``fk_policy`` and the verbs does not matter.  It checks
        ``USUBJID`` against the pinned ``DM`` (SDTM) or ``ADSL`` (ADaM),
        and the SDTM trial-design keys of ``_FK_RULES`` against a pinned
        TA, TE or TV.

        Args:
            severity: One of ``"warn"`` (emit ``UserWarning``),
                ``"error"`` (raise ``DerivationError``), or ``"off"``
                (disable FK checks).

        Returns:
            Self: A shallow copy with the updated policy.

        Examples:
            Enforce strict FK checking::

                ae = (
                    ae_raw.sdtm
                    .pin("DM", dm_df)
                    .fk_policy("error")
                    .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        if severity not in ("warn", "error", "off"):
            raise DerivationError(
                f"fk_policy severity must be 'warn', 'error', or 'off', got '{severity}'"
            )
        new = copy.copy(self)
        new._fk_severity = severity
        return new

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Internal helpers (used by verbs)                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _require_pin(
        self,
        domain: str,
        verb: str,
        columns: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Retrieve a pinned DataFrame or raise an actionable error.

        The calling verb records the read with ``record_pin_lineage()``.

        Args:
            domain: Upper-cased domain name (e.g. ``"DM"``).
            verb: Name of the calling verb (for error messages and lineage).
            columns: If specified, return only these columns plus the
                join key — surgical extraction.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: The pinned (or sliced) DataFrame.

        Raises:
            PinError: If the domain is not pinned, with an actionable
                message telling the user what to add.  Also catchable as
                ``LookupError``.
        """
        pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = getattr(self, "_pinned", {})
        key = domain.upper()
        if key not in pinned:
            raise PinError(
                f"{verb}() requires a pinned '{key}' domain. "
                f'Add .pin("{key}", {key.lower()}_df) before .{verb}() in your chain.'
            )
        df, join_key = pinned[key]
        if columns is not None:
            needed = list(dict.fromkeys(join_key + columns))
            df = df.select([c for c in needed if c in df.columns])
        return df

    def _pin_join_key(self, domain: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return the stored join key for a pinned domain.

        Args:
            domain: Upper-cased domain name.

        Raises:
            PinError: If *domain* is not pinned.  Also catchable as
                ``LookupError``.
        """
        pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = getattr(self, "_pinned", {})
        key = domain.upper()
        if key not in pinned:
            raise PinError(f"No pin found for domain '{key}'.")
        return list(pinned[key][1])

    def _run_fk_checks(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        """Check the foreign keys of the final frame *df* against the pins.

        Called by the public ``to_frame()`` only, with the ``fk_policy`` in
        force on this namespace.  Each ``_FK_RULES`` column of *df* with a
        pinned reference is checked once.  A
        warning is given once per namespace; an error raises on every call.
        """
        severity = getattr(self, "_fk_severity", "warn")
        if severity == "off":
            return
        rules: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = self.__class__._FK_RULES
        pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = getattr(self, "_pinned", {})
        warned: frozenset[str] = getattr(self, "_fk_warned", frozenset())
        for col, rule in rules.items():
            if col not in df.columns:
                continue
            pin = rule.get("pin", "").upper()
            ref_col = rule.get("ref_col", col)
            if pin not in pinned or ref_col not in pinned[pin][0].columns:
                continue
            ref_df = pinned[pin][0]
            current_vals = set(df[col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
            ref_vals = set(ref_df[ref_col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
            orphans = current_vals - ref_vals - set(rule.get("allow", "").split())
            if not orphans:
                continue
            msg = (
                f"FK check: {len(orphans)} value(s) in '{col}' not found in "
                f"pinned {pin}.{ref_col}: {sorted(orphans)[:5]}"
            )
            if rule.get("note"):
                msg += f". {rule['note']}"
            if severity == "error" and rule.get("max_severity") != "warn":
                raise DerivationError(msg)
            if msg not in warned:
                # Rebind, never mutate: earlier chain copies keep their own memo.
                warned = warned | {msg}
                self._fk_warned = warned
                warnings.warn(msg, stacklevel=3)

    def pin(
    self,
    domain: str | None = None,
    df: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
    **frames: pl.DataFrame,
) -> Self:
    """Attach one or more reference domains to this pipeline.

    Two equivalent forms, usable together — the keyword form declares
    every upstream dataset in one call (kwarg name = dataset name),
    mirroring the define.yaml ``inputs:`` block:

    * ``pin("DM", dm_df)`` — one pin, positional.
    * ``pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df)`` — several pins, one call.

    The name/frame pair is positional-only, so *every* keyword except
    ``join_on`` is a dataset pin — no dataset name is reserved.

    Args:
        domain: Logical name (e.g. ``"DM"``, ``"ADSL"``, ``"TV"``).
        df: The reference DataFrame for *domain*.  A LazyFrame is
            collected once, at pin time.
        join_on: Column(s) used to join these references into the
            pipeline.  Applies to every pin in this call; pin
            separately for per-domain join keys.
        **frames: ``NAME=frame`` pins (names are upper-cased).

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the pin(s) attached; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When called with no pins, a name without its
            frame (or vice versa), or a pinned value that is not a
            DataFrame/LazyFrame.

    Examples:
        Pin DM to an AE pipeline for study-day derivation::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .assign("DOMAIN", value="AE")
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Declare every upstream dataset of an ADaM pipeline at once::

            adae = (
                ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
                .pin(ADSL=adsl_df, EX=ex_df)
                .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "SAFFL")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    pins: dict[str, pl.DataFrame] = {}
    if domain is not None or df is not None:
        if domain is None or df is None:
            raise DerivationError(
                "pin() requires both a domain name and a DataFrame — "
                'pin("DM", dm_df) — or keyword pins: pin(DM=dm_df).'
            )
        pins[domain] = df
    pins.update(frames)
    if not pins:
        raise DerivationError(
            'pin() requires at least one pin: pin("DM", dm_df) or pin(DM=dm_df, ADSL=adsl_df).'
        )

    new = copy.copy(self)
    pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = dict(getattr(self, "_pinned", {}))
    for name, frame in pins.items():
        frame = _pin_frame(name, frame)
        key = name.upper()
        if key in pinned:
            warnings.warn(
                f"Pin '{key}' replaced. Use .repin() to suppress this warning.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        pinned[key] = (frame, _normalize_key(join_on))
    new._pinned = pinned
    return new

    def repin(
    self,
    domain: str,
    df: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    join_on: str | list[str] = "USUBJID",
) -> Self:
    """Replace an existing pin explicitly (no warning).

    Args:
        domain: Logical name to replace.
        df: The new reference DataFrame.  A LazyFrame is collected
            once, at pin time.
        join_on: Column(s) for the join key.

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the pin replaced.

    Raises:
        DerivationError: When *df* is not a DataFrame or LazyFrame.

    Examples:
        Replace a previously pinned DM with a filtered version::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .pin("DM", dm_full)
                .repin("DM", dm_filtered)
                .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    new = copy.copy(self)
    pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = dict(getattr(self, "_pinned", {}))
    pinned[domain.upper()] = (_pin_frame(domain, df), _normalize_key(join_on))
    new._pinned = pinned
    return new

    def pins(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Inspect currently pinned domains.

    Returns:
        dict: ``{domain: {"df": DataFrame, "join_on": [cols]}}``.

    Examples:
        Check what's pinned before study_day::

            ns = ae_raw.sdtm.pin("DM", dm_df).pin("TV", tv_df, join_on="VISITNUM")
            print(ns.pins())
            # {'DM': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['USUBJID']},
            #  'TV': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['VISITNUM']}}
    """
    pinned: dict[str, tuple[pl.DataFrame, list[str]]] = getattr(self, "_pinned", {})
    return {domain: {"df": df, "join_on": list(key)} for domain, (df, key) in pinned.items()}

    fk_policy(severity)

    Set the FK-check severity for this pipeline.

    The check runs once, at the public to_frame() (and the terminal verbs that call it), on the final frame, with the severity in force at that point. The order of pin, fk_policy and the verbs does not matter. It checks USUBJID against the pinned DM (SDTM) or ADSL (ADaM), and the SDTM trial-design keys of _FK_RULES against a pinned TA, TE or TV.

    def fk_policy(self, severity: str) -> Self:
    """Set the FK-check severity for this pipeline.

    The check runs once, at the public ``to_frame()`` (and the
    terminal verbs that call it), on the final frame, with the
    severity in force at that point.  The order of ``pin``,
    ``fk_policy`` and the verbs does not matter.  It checks
    ``USUBJID`` against the pinned ``DM`` (SDTM) or ``ADSL`` (ADaM),
    and the SDTM trial-design keys of ``_FK_RULES`` against a pinned
    TA, TE or TV.

    Args:
        severity: One of ``"warn"`` (emit ``UserWarning``),
            ``"error"`` (raise ``DerivationError``), or ``"off"``
            (disable FK checks).

    Returns:
        Self: A shallow copy with the updated policy.

    Examples:
        Enforce strict FK checking::

            ae = (
                ae_raw.sdtm
                .pin("DM", dm_df)
                .fk_policy("error")
                .assign("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    if severity not in ("warn", "error", "off"):
        raise DerivationError(
            f"fk_policy severity must be 'warn', 'error', or 'off', got '{severity}'"
        )
    new = copy.copy(self)
    new._fk_severity = severity
    return new

    Exceptions¶

    fleet.core.exceptions ¶

    Core exceptions for fleet.

    The verb-layer exceptions use dual inheritance so both catch styles work: except FleetError (the Fleet-native style) and the legacy builtin style (except ValueError / except TypeError / except LookupError) that predates the hierarchy.

    • :class:DerivationError — a verb received invalid values or arguments (missing column, unparseable expression, unsupported option, ...). Catchable as ValueError.
    • :class:VerbUsageError — a verb was called with a wrong type. Catchable as TypeError.
    • :class:PinError — a cross-domain verb could not resolve a pinned reference domain. Catchable as LookupError.
